item.title: TT-104: Undo for tasktracker.store.TaskStore
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The tasktracker library lives in the `tasktracker/` package at the repo root; tests are in `tests/`. Standard library only. Run tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; existing tests must keep passing and you must add tests for this change. Commit only this ticket's change, as one commit, with a clear message (`TT-104: ...`). Do not add any attribution lines (no "Generated by Claude", no Co-Authored-By). Do not change git identity. This item is stacked on TT-103's branch; keep its changes intact.

Ticket TT-104 (implement exactly):

`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:

- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Keep functions under 60 lines, add meaningful assertions/validation at the boundary, and do not hide failures.

item.title: TT-103: Query syntax for tasktracker.search.search
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The tasktracker library lives in the `tasktracker/` package at the repo root; tests are in `tests/`. Standard library only. Run tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; existing tests must keep passing and you must add tests for this change. Commit only this ticket's change, as one commit, with a clear message (`TT-103: ...`). Do not add any attribution lines (no "Generated by Claude", no Co-Authored-By). Do not change git identity. This item is stacked on TT-102's branch; keep its changes intact.

Ticket TT-103 (implement exactly):

`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:

- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Keep functions under 60 lines, add meaningful assertions/validation at the boundary, and do not hide failures.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export in tasktracker.export.to_csv
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The tasktracker library lives in the `tasktracker/` package at the repo root; tests are in `tests/`. Standard library only. Run tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; existing tests must keep passing and you must add tests for this change. This item is stacked on TT-101's branch; keep its changes intact.

Ticket TT-102 (implement exactly):

`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:

- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

Keep functions under 60 lines, add meaningful assertions/validation at the boundary, and do not hide failures.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in tasktracker.dates.parse_due
item.brief:
Repository: long-backlog. The tasktracker library lives in the `tasktracker/` package at the repo root; tests are in `tests/`. Standard library only. Run tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; existing tests must keep passing and you must add tests for this change. Commit only this ticket's change, as one commit, with a clear message (`TT-101: ...`). Do not add any attribution lines (no "Generated by Claude", no Co-Authored-By). Do not change git identity.

Ticket TT-101 (implement exactly):

`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:

- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Keep functions under 60 lines, add meaningful assertions/validation at the boundary, and do not hide failures.

state.summary:
TT-101 implemented in one commit, ee2c734 ("TT-101: Reject impossible due dates in parse_due"), on archon/0tpe4ctt-tt-101-reject-impossible-due-dates-in-ta. Not pushed.

What changed: tasktracker/dates.py now defines InvalidDate(ValueError). parse_due raises it for impossible calendar dates (message contains the original text), for any unmatched form, and for offsets that overflow the date range. Negative and unsigned offsets (-3d, 3d) are rejected. +0d returns today. today/tomorrow, case-insensitivity and whitespace trimming are unchanged. The clamping is gone and the unused calendar import removed. tests/test_basic.py gains tests for impossible dates, leap-day acceptance, malformed input, +0d, and InvalidDate being a ValueError.
